Record date: 2129-11-14
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/14/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Continued cough with yellow sputum, increased shortness of breath, and persistent fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for a follow-up visit one week after the initiation of oral Levofloxacin and continuation of oral Prednisone for his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation. He reports that while there has been a slight reduction in the frequency of his cough, it remains productive with yellow sputum. However, he notes a concerning increase in shortness of breath, particularly during minimal exertion. The patient describes a feeling of tightness in his chest and states that his fatigue has not improved, impacting his ability to perform daily activities. He denies any new onset of fever or hemoptysis but expresses frustration over the lack of significant progress.
Mr. Fairfax has been diligent in adhering to his medication regimen and has continued using nebulized albuterol as prescribed. He reports that his symptom diary reflects a pattern of persistent symptoms, with no notable changes in the nature of his sputum.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent productive cough with yellow sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 134/80 mmHg - Heart Rate: 80 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 28 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 86% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued, with labored breathing noted.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Marked wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with audible rhonchi.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with ongoing exacerbation; insufficient response to current treatment evidenced by persistent cough, increased dyspnea, and fatigue. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload. 3. Persistent fatigue likely multifactorial, exacerbated by respiratory symptoms and potential deconditioning.
PLAN
1. Discontinue Levofloxacin due to lack of clinical improvement and consider the possibility of a viral infection or atypical pneumonia; initiate a course of oral Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 10 days to cover potential bacterial pathogens. 2. Continue oral Prednisone 20 mg daily for an additional 5 days to manage inflammation associated with COPD exacerbation. 3. Increase the dose of Salmeterol to 50 mcg twice daily and add Tiotropium 18 mcg once daily to enhance bronchodilation and improve respiratory function. 4. Continue nebulized albuterol every hour as needed; advise Mr. Fairfax to monitor and report any increased frequency of use or side effects. 5. Schedule follow-up in one week for reevaluation of respiratory status, sputum characteristics, and overall fatigue levels. If symptoms do not show significant improvement, consider referral to pulmonary specialist and pulmonary function testing.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with a revised prescription for oral Doxycycline and continued Prednisone therapy. He was advised to maintain his symptom diary and to utilize nebulized albuterol as needed. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for one week from today to assess the effectiveness of the new treatment regimen and to further refine his management plan based on clinical response.
